Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sysPrep (development version)

  • Behavior change: link_encounters() now stops with an error when ed_data and inpatient_admission_data carry different HasBeen_ flag columns (for example HasBeenAdmitted in one pull and only HasBeenI in the other). The other pull’s rows would hold NA in a flag that ESSENCE never leaves missing, which silently corrupted flag counts and the admission-flag choice. Query both pulls with the same HasBeen_ fields. A call that previously ran on mismatched pulls now errors; calls whose pulls match are unchanged. The documentation gains a “Required fields” section listing what each pull must carry.
  • New message: with verbose = TRUE, link_encounters() reports how many episodes hold more than one record from the same pull (the same facility and visit more than once in a pull), which are merged into one episode; run dedupe() on each pull first. It changes no output.
  • Wording: the package description and the encounter-linkage vignette title now say “improved burden estimation” rather than “accurate”.
  • Behavior change: link_encounters() now keeps the most severe DispositionCategory in a linked episode, whichever record carries it. The default strategy for that field is the new "prefer_severity" (replacing "prefer_admission"): DECEASED ranks above TRANSFERRED, which ranks above DISCHARGED and ADMIT (equal), which rank above UNKNOWN and a missing value. Previously the first admission-class row’s value won, so an ED record that also carried HasBeenAdmitted = 1 and read DISCHARGED could hide a death or transfer on the linked inpatient record. When the merged value is DECEASED, C_Death is also set to affirmative for that linked episode ("Yes" for ESSENCE’s own Yes/No; "1" or 1 when the column is already 0/1, read from the whole column so a text "0"/"1" column stays 0/1). This derives C_Death from the category, so it can change a "No" that both records carried, and a record that is not linked is never changed. Equally severe values (ADMIT and DISCHARGED) resolve to the inpatient pull’s record, which reflects the whole encounter of care: an ED ADMIT gives way to the inpatient record’s DISCHARGED, and the result does not depend on whether the ED record also carries HasBeenAdmitted. Discharge_Disposition now uses the new "follow_severity" strategy: it takes the value from the same record that supplied DispositionCategory, so the two fields agree whenever that record has a value (when it has none, the "prefer_admission" value is used and the two can differ). Episodes whose records agree are unchanged. To keep the old behavior, pass merge_fields with "prefer_admission" for these fields.
  • Bug fix: link_encounters() split a record with a missing facility_col or visit_col value into one visit per patient class (an "ED" row and an "Admitted" row from one HasBeenE = 1, HasBeenAdmitted = 1 record became two collapsed rows, counted twice). The record now stays one episode, and the missing-key message counts records. Records with a single patient class, and every record with a key, are unchanged; only the numeric suffix of .episode_id after such a record can shift.
  • Bug fix: numeric identifiers of 16 or more digits were written in scientific notation and rounded when held as text, so two different Visit_ID values could link as one visit in link_encounters(). Whole numbers are now written in full. filter_care_setting() uses the same conversion, so a numeric fix_facility_id_vector containing round numbers such as 100000 (which as.character() writes as "1e+05") now matches a text Hospital column instead of silently matching nothing.
  • Improvement: when ed_data and inpatient_admission_data hold the same column in incompatible types, link_encounters() now stops with a message that names the function and the two pulls instead of a bind_rows() error.
  • Documentation: review_facility_ed_visits() now states that visits_per_day is the count divided by one number of days for every facility, so it flags the same facilities as raw counts and adds the unit (it makes pulls of different durations comparable); it does not by itself improve dropout detection. link_encounters() states that every row of inpatient_admission_data is labeled "Direct Admit" whatever its own C_Patient_Class_List says, and recommends reading key columns as text. assign_treating_geography()’s @return says when region_col is overwritten. .episode_n_rows is documented as the number of patient-class rows (a record carrying several classes counts once per class), not the number of records, so it should not be used on its own to count linked episodes.

sysPrep 0.1.0

  • Bug fix: clean_names = FALSE now returns the input’s own column names in filter_care_setting(), link_encounters(), assign_treating_geography(), assign_facility_geography(), and review_facility_ed_visits(); it previously still returned snake_case names (only dedupe() honored it). Columns the function adds keep their own names.
  • Bug fix: review_facility_ed_visits() normalized visits_per_day by the days that facility sent data, so a facility that stopped sending partway through the pull scored the same as one that sent every day. It now divides by the number of distinct dates in the whole pull (n_days still reports the facility’s own days). .outlier_method now records the criterion that fired ("percentile", "iqr", or "percentile+iqr") instead of echoing the method argument. The documentation now says that method = "percentile" ranks the tails: with the default thresholds it flags the lowest and highest facility in a small pull whether or not either is abnormal; method = "iqr" flags only values outside the spread.
  • Bug fix: filter_care_setting(fix_facility_type_regex = ) no longer overwrites the facility type with NA for a row whose facility name is missing (which then dropped the row at the keep_types step) or lists NA as a matched facility.
  • Bug fix: assign_facility_geography() no longer requires the patient Region and ZipCode columns, which it never reads when every row is reassigned; without them it previously skipped that geography type with a misleading “not found” message.
  • Bug fix: .index_encounter in link_encounters(return_format = "long") now marks exactly one row per episode: the first "ED" row, else the first row (the same row the collapsed output is built from). It could previously be absent (a multi-row episode with no ED row, or an NA class) or repeated (two ED rows), so long-format counts disagreed with the collapsed row count. Collapsed output is unaffected (the column is TRUE there). No other column of link_encounters() output changes.
  • Bug fix: link_encounters() now aborts when the linking columns (facility_col, visit_col, and fallback_visit_col) are missing from inpatient_admission_data, where it previously linked nothing without a message.
  • New argument: dedupe() and summarize_duplicates() gain verbose (default TRUE), so the missing-key message can be silenced as in every other function that reports messages.
  • Behavior change: link_encounters() now holds its linking keys, the facility column (default Hospital), visit_col (default Visit_ID) and fallback_visit_col, as text in the output, whatever type each pull delivered them in. These identifiers have no numeric meaning, and a CSV read can return one pull’s keys as numbers and the other’s as text, which previously failed in bind_rows(). Numbers are written in full (100000, not 1e+05). Keys that were already text (as the ESSENCE dataDetails API returns them) are unchanged; a numeric Hospital now comes back as text, so convert it back after the call if you need numbers. .episode_id is unchanged. dedupe(), summarize_duplicates() and classify_duplicates() already compared these keys as text and still return each column in the type it arrived in.
  • Bug fix: the "concat" merge strategy in link_encounters() skipped a value whenever it appeared anywhere inside the text already collected, even inside a longer word or code, so detail present in only one record could be lost ("fall" inside "waterfall", the diagnosis code "R10.9" inside "R10.90"). It now treats a value as already present only when it appears as whole words or whole codes (ignoring case, punctuation and spacing), so complaint text, diagnosis codes and SNOMED codes found in one record but not the other are kept. "concat" is not in the default merge_fields.
  • Performance: link_encounters() builds its episode metadata with whole-column operations rather than a per-episode call, several times faster on a 290,000-row pull with identical output; dedupe(keep = "most_complete") counts each row’s non-missing values once instead of once per group.
  • Documentation: dedupe()’s visit_col no longer lists patient-level identifiers (C_Unique_Patient_ID, MRN) as alternatives, and its example using one is removed: they are shared by all of a patient’s visits, so using one collapses repeat visits. dedupe() also documents that a row with a missing order_by value sorts last. The documentation also now states that fallback_visit_col only links two rows that are both missing visit_col; that .patient_class_sequence lists classes with identical or missing timestamps alphabetically, which carries no clinical meaning; that assign_treating_geography() takes the site prefix from site rather than parsing it from the data; that .out_of_state is TRUE for another state, OTHER_REGION, {site}_UNKNOWN, and a missing Region; that the percent in classify_duplicates()$overall is the share of duplicated visit groups; and that n_biosense_ids is reported but not used to classify. Wording that claimed more than the code establishes (“approximating both residence-based and incidence-based burden”, “a close approximation of hospital-level cluster detection”) was softened.
  • Input validation: every exported function now checks its arguments up front and aborts with a message that names the offending argument. This covers a non-data-frame data (or ed_data/inpatient_admission_data); a TRUE/FALSE switch (verbose, clean_names, overwrite, …) that is NA or not length 1; a percentile_low/percentile_high outside [0, 1] or reversed, or a negative iqr_multiplier, in review_facility_ed_visits(); a non-character keep_types, fix_to, or fix_facility_type_regex in filter_care_setting(); and a non-string site or output column name in the geography functions. A malformed merge_fields in link_encounters() (for example an unnamed vector, which was previously ignored without a message) now aborts too. Errors are attributed to the exported function the user called rather than an internal helper, and choice arguments (keep, method, return_format) report their valid values through rlang::arg_match().
  • Bug fix: assign_treating_geography() now warns when no Region value begins with the site prefix (for example site = "ky", since matching is case-sensitive, or a pull from a different state than site). Previously every visit was silently flagged as out-of-state.
  • Behavior change: print() for essence_dup_summary and essence_dup_classified objects now writes the whole report to standard output, through new format() methods, instead of splitting it between the message and output streams. capture.output(), sink(), and knitr now see the complete report.
  • Interface change: dedupe()’s signature now shows keep’s valid values (c("first", "last", "most_complete"); the default is still "first"), and link_encounters()’s signature no longer shows a misleading inpatient_admission_data = NULL default. The argument was already required: omitting it, or passing NULL, aborts with the same message as before.
  • Documentation: parameters shared by several functions (data, facility_col, visit_col, clean_names, verbose, the geography column arguments, and others) are now documented once and inherited with @inheritParams, so their wording can no longer drift between help pages. The format() and print() methods for essence_dup_summary and essence_dup_classified are documented on ?summarize_duplicates and ?classify_duplicates. Internal helpers are documented for maintainers (for example ?resolve_col, ?key_has_na_mask, ?merge_strategies); they are marked @keywords internal, so they do not appear in the reference index.
  • Internal: removed collapse_episode(), an unused earlier implementation of the episode-collapsing step in link_encounters(), and reorganized the helpers into thematic R/utils-*.R files. The long exported functions are now short pipelines over documented stage helpers, each group on one help page that lists the stages in order: link_encounters() (?check_inpatient_admission_data), review_facility_ed_visits() (?check_percentile_order), filter_care_setting() (?apply_type_correction), the two geography functions (?validate_geography_cols), classify_duplicates() (?resolve_classification_cols), and dedupe()/summarize_duplicates() (?sort_for_dedupe). link_encounters() went from 580 lines at cyclomatic complexity 49 to 97 lines at complexity 6. The restructuring itself changes no function’s output, messages, or warnings; the behavior changes are the separate items listed above.
  • Dependencies: the minimum dplyr version is now 1.2.0, the release that added dplyr::recode_values(), which link_encounters() already used. stats and utils are now declared in Imports.
  • New feature: link_encounters() gains an optional fallback_visit_col argument. By default (NULL), a row missing visit_col is never merged with another row solely because they share that same missing value (see the NA-key bug fix below); correct in general, but it means a real split episode (an ED row and a direct-admit row for the same visit) with Visit_ID missing on both sides is left as two unmatched rows instead of one linked episode, since visit_col alone can’t confirm they match. fallback_visit_col names a secondary identifier (e.g. C_BioSense_ID, observed in real production data to be assigned identically to both rows of such a split episode even when Visit_ID is missing on both) to use for that specific case: a row missing visit_col is matched to another row sharing facility_col and the same fallback_visit_col value instead of being left unmatchable. Rows with a real visit_col value are never affected, and omitting the argument preserves the original NA-key behavior exactly. Reported against real production data in a downstream ETL pipeline (149 real split episodes sharing a missing Visit_ID and a matching C_BioSense_ID, confirmed via distinct() after dropping the differing HasBeen_-derived field).
  • Bug fix: classify_duplicates() no longer emits a spurious base R warning (“replacement element 1 has 1 row to replace 0 rows”) on a genuinely clean pull with zero duplicates. janitor::adorn_pct_formatting() errors on a 0-row tabyl; $overall is now built directly as an empty tibble in that case instead of being routed through it.
  • Bug fix: dedupe(), summarize_duplicates(), classify_duplicates(), and link_encounters() no longer collapse rows that share a missing facility_col or visit_col value into a single group. dplyr::group_by() (and .by =) follow SQL’s GROUP BY convention of treating every NA as equal to every other NA for grouping purposes, even though NA == NA evaluates to NA everywhere else in R. A missing identifier means a row’s true identity is unknown, not confirmed to match every other row with a missing identifier. Previously, several rows sharing a missing Visit_ID at the same facility were silently treated as one duplicated visit: dedupe() discarded all but one of them, summarize_duplicates()/classify_duplicates() reported them as duplicated when they weren’t, and link_encounters() ran its episode-reconciliation logic (has_been_ flag max(), field merging) across genuinely unrelated visits sharing one synthesized .episode_id. Each of these functions now treats a row with a missing key as its own distinct record and emits an informational message (rlang::inform(), suppressible via verbose = FALSE where that argument exists) reporting how many rows were affected.
  • Behavior change: dedupe(), summarize_duplicates(), classify_duplicates(), review_facility_ed_visits(), and link_encounters() now prefer Hospital/C_BioSense_Facility_ID over HospitalName as the default facility_col, whenever Hospital is present in the data, falling back to HospitalName only if it isn’t. Hospital is a stable numeric identifier; HospitalName is a display string that changes on a facility rename or rebrand, so grouping by name can silently split one facility’s rows into two across a rename, or merge two different facilities that briefly share a display name. An explicitly supplied facility_col always overrides this preference exactly as given. filter_care_setting()‘s facility_col is deliberately unchanged, since it matches against fix_facility_type_vector’s exact facility name strings; that function already exposes a separate, ID-preferring facility_id_col/fix_facility_id_vector for the same durability benefit. If you have code that assumes dedupe() (or the other affected functions) group by HospitalName/hospital_name by default, and your data includes Hospital, update it to reference hospital/Hospital instead, or pass facility_col = HospitalName explicitly to keep the old behavior. The five affected functions’ facility_col argument now defaults to NULL (was a fixed column name) so that args()/the Usage line accurately reflect that the real default is resolved at runtime rather than printing a fixed default that’s no longer accurate; this matches how order_by/date_col already behave elsewhere in the package.
  • Bug fix in link_encounters(): when deriving patient_class from HasBeen_ flags (the fallback path used when C_Patient_Class_List is absent), the has_been_e/has_been_admitted/etc. columns were silently lost from the output for any row that never came from inpatient_admission_data directly, showing as NA on single-row episodes, and, worse, as an incorrectly reconciled value (e.g. has_been_e = 0 on a merged episode that genuinely included an ED visit) on multi-row merged episodes. link_encounters() now preserves each row’s true original HasBeen_ values across the pivot, so every episode shows correct 0/1 values, never NA, and never an incorrect reconciled value.
  • Bug fix in link_encounters(): in the same HasBeen_-flag fallback path, when ed_data contained both HasBeenAdmitted and HasBeenI, HasBeenI was dropped from ed_data entirely to keep it from contributing a redundant “Admitted” row to the patient-class pivot, which discarded its real 0/1 values for every ed_data row. After bind_rows() with inpatient_admission_data, only rows sourced from the inpatient pull retained a real has_been_i value; every ED-pull row showed NA. HasBeenI is now excluded from the pivot without being removed from the data, so its true value is preserved on every row.
  • The message issued when HasBeenO = 1 visits are present is now an informational message (suppressible via verbose = FALSE) rather than a warning, and no longer implies these visits will show patient_class = "Outpatient" in the default collapsed output; they won’t, whenever the same episode also includes an ED or inpatient-admission record (the norm for link_encounters()’s two-pull input), since only the primary row’s patient_class survives collapsing. HasBeenO = 1 is ordinary co-occurring ESSENCE data, not a data quality concern.
  • Added CITATION.cff (Citation File Format) at the package root for GitHub’s “Cite this repository” feature and Zenodo DOI metadata, alongside the existing inst/CITATION used by citation("sysPrep").
  • Designed for ESSENCE dataDetails pulls from the NSSP ESSENCE va_er (Patient Location, Full Details) and va_hosp (Facility Location, Full Details) data sources, which the package was developed and tested against.
  • dedupe(): Remove duplicate ESSENCE records with flexible keep strategy.
  • summarize_duplicates(): Summarize duplicate counts by facility.
  • classify_duplicates(): Classify duplication mechanism by type. Supports verbose to suppress informational messages.
  • filter_care_setting(): Filter to valid emergency and inpatient care settings. Supports verbose to suppress informational messages, and fix_facility_id_vector to correct known facilities by their stable Hospital/C_BioSense_Facility_ID value, more durable across facility name changes than fix_facility_type_vector.
  • link_encounters(): Link ED and inpatient encounters into care episodes, merging each episode’s rows into one composite row by default (return_format = "collapsed"); HasBeen_ flags reconciled via max, and CCDD/CCDDParsed/CCDDCategory_flat/C_Death/ Discharge_Disposition/DispositionCategory reconciled via configurable merge_fields strategies. return_format = "long" preserves the prior unmerged output. Supports verbose to suppress informational messages. Breaking: inpatient_admission_data is now required; the prior single-pull mode (ed_data alone) could not detect a genuine direct admission (structurally absent from a HasBeenE = 1 pull) and was a no-op on an already-deduplicated ED-to-inpatient escalation, so link_encounters() now aborts with an actionable message instead of silently returning ed_data unchanged. Query a second ESSENCE pull filtered to HasBeenAdmitted = 1 (or HasBeenI = 1), deduplicate it separately, and pass it as inpatient_admission_data.
  • Added essence_ed_raw and essence_inp_raw: two small synthetic datasets representing separately queried HasBeenE = 1 and HasBeenAdmitted = 1 ESSENCE pulls, used by vignette("encounter-linkage") and link_encounters()’s own examples to demonstrate two-pull linkage. essence_raw/essence_clean are unchanged by this and continue to represent a single realistic ED pull.
  • review_facility_ed_visits(): Flag facility visit count outliers for QA. Supports verbose to suppress informational messages.
  • assign_treating_geography(): Assign treating facility geography to out-of-state visits. By default writes to new new_region_col/ new_zip_col columns ("region_hybrid"/"zip_code_hybrid"), leaving region_col/zip_col untouched; set overwrite = TRUE to overwrite them in place instead. Supports verbose to suppress informational messages.
  • assign_facility_geography(): Assign facility geography to all visits. Same new_region_col/new_zip_col/overwrite behavior as assign_treating_geography(), defaulting to "region_facility"/ "zip_code_facility". Supports verbose to suppress informational messages.
